Which two nuclei are isotopes of the same element?
A
P and Q
B
P and S
C
Q and R
D
R and S

hints: Notice the table gives number of neutrons and nucleon number $A$, not proton number $Z$ directly.
Recall isotopes have the same number of protons, where proton number $Z = $ nucleon number $-$ number of neutrons.
Calculate $Z$ for P, Q, R and S and look for the pair with equal $Z$ but different neutron numbers.
walkthrough: Isotopes are nuclei of the same element, so they must have the same proton number $Z$ but different numbers of neutrons.
Use $Z = A - N$ where $A$ is nucleon number and $N$ is number of neutrons from the table.
Only R and S share the same $Z = 8$, while their neutron numbers $6$ and $8$ differ, which is the condition for isotopes.

A.explanation: P has $10-5=5$ protons and Q has $10-6=4$ protons, so different proton number means different elements.

B.explanation: P has $5$ protons and S has $16-8=8$ protons, so they cannot be isotopes of the same element.

C.explanation: Q has $4$ protons and R has $14-6=8$ protons, so same neutron number alone does not make isotopes.

D.explanation: R and S both have $8$ protons but $6$ and $8$ neutrons respectively, so same proton number with different neutron number.
